sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Strings are everywhere in programming - from user input to file handling. Today, you'll master the essential String class methods that make text manipulation a breeze!

• How to use common String methods like `length()`, `charAt()`, and `substring()`
• The magic of string concatenation and comparison
• Practical ways to transform and search strings

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine strings as a row of connected train cars. Each car holds one character, and you can:
- Count how many cars there are (length)
- Peek inside any car (charAt)
- Take a segment of cars (substring)

Strings in Java are objects with powerful built-in tools (methods) to work with text. Unlike primitive types, they come with their own set of superpowers!

• **Immutable**: Once created, strings can't be changed (but you can create new ones)
• **Zero-indexed**: First character is at position 0, not 1
• **Method-rich**: Over 50 useful methods available at your fingertips

sections.title: Code Examples
examples:
String s = "Welcome to Java";

System.out.println(s.length());           // 15
System.out.println(s.charAt(0));          // W
System.out.println(s.indexOf("Java"));    // 11
System.out.println(s.substring(11));      // Java
System.out.println(s.replace("Java", "Python")); // Welcome to Python
System.out.println(s.toUpperCase());      // WELCOME TO JAVA
System.out.println(s.trim());             // removes leading/trailing spaces
System.out.println(s.contains("come"));   // true

sections.title: Key Points
points: length() returns the number of characters in the string
charAt(index) returns the character at the specified position
substring(begin, end) returns characters from begin to end-1
indexOf() and lastIndexOf() find the position of a character or substring
compareTo() compares strings lexicographically; equals() checks content equality

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Strings are objects with powerful built-in methods for text manipulation. Most important methods: `length()`, `charAt()`, `substring()`, `equals()`, `contains()`. Practice combining methods for more complex operations. Ready to learn about `StringBuilder` for more efficient string modifications.

questions.question: What does the substring(2, 5) method return for the string "HelloWorld"?
questions.explanation: substring(2, 5) returns characters from index 2 (inclusive) to index 5 (exclusive). For "HelloWorld", indices 2, 3, 4 are 'l', 'l', 'o', giving "llo".

questions.question: What does the indexOf("Java") method return if the substring is not found?
questions.explanation: The indexOf() method returns -1 if the specified substring is not found in the string. If found, it returns the index of the first occurrence.
